newsitem.title: CANADA: PanCanadian starts up NGL extraction plant.
newsitem.headline: PanCanadian starts up NGL extraction plant.

text.p: PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd said on Thursday its new natural gas liquids extraction plant near Empress, Alberta was operational and had operated at its licensed capacity.

The plant, which is also owned by Alberta Energy Co Ltd Renaissance Energy Ltd and Anderson Exploration Ltd, was designed to extract gas liquids such as propane, butane and pentanes plus from the natural gas stream.
At capacity, it would process 800 million cubic feet of gas per day, producing about 8,000 barrels of NGLs per day.

From Empress, which is near the Alberta-Saskatchewan border, the liquids are transported to fractionation facilities in Ontario and Michigan via IPL Energy Inc's Interprovincial and Lakehead pipelines.
PanCanadian said commissioning of the C$72-million plant was completed on September 1.
The Empress plant is one of several initiatives being undertaken by Canadian producers to realize higher prices for their natural gas liquids.
PanCanadian and AEC both have a 40-percent interest in the project. Renaissance and Anderson hold 10 percent each.
